PagerDuty Bot: 🔔 ALERT: service="inference-prod" escalated to escalation_policy="sre-oncall-policy" — trigger=error_rate_spike — incident: https://pd.redwood.example/i/INC12345

IncidentBot: @channel page fired to SRE-OnCall (priority: P1). Auto-escalation scheduled in 5m if unacked.

Alice M: acked. I'm seeing the page went to the SRE policy but this incident looks like a routing mistake — customer-impacting error from model serving that should route to Platform-Oncall first.

Ben K: wait, why would inference-prod be bound to sre-oncall-policy? we moved that service last quarter. Lemme check bindings.

Carla G: quick heads up: I noticed a shadow schedule entry for "platform-oncall" where an external contractor account shares the same email alias as an SRE rota user. PD resolves by user email and recently a schedule cursor override was applied. Could be related.

SRE OnCall: getting multiple duplicate pages. I only saw the SRE policy because PD matched the email on the schedule entry. I'm taking lead but think this should be platform.

Alice M: can someone paste the PD service config? suspicious that escalation_policy points to the old SRE policy.

Ben K: config dump: ```
service: inference-prod
escalation_policy: sre-oncall-policy
alert_rules:
  - error_rate > 3% for 2m
  - latency_p95 > 1200ms
bindings:
  - team: platform-team (should be)
  - owner: alice@redwood.example
```

Carla G: here's the schedule diff I pulled: ```
schedule: platform-oncall
overrides:
  - start: 2025-08-01
    end: 2026-08-01
    override_by: manager-override@redwood.example
    note: emergency coverage
users:
  - ben.k@redwood.example
  - shared.alias@redwood.example  # this is the contractor alias
```

Alice M: yup — PD is resolving the schedule entry to the contractor alias and then applying the escalation policy that user is currently a member of. So pages go to SRE by accident. This is a misconfigured schedule+service binding combo.

IncidentBot: escalation notice — incident INC12345 escalated to level 2 at 3m 20s (auto-escalation).

SRE OnCall: I'm going to quiet the PD service -> applying a temporary silence for 30m to stop the noise while we fix routing. Executing: `pd service silence create inference-prod --duration 30m --reason "routing loop"`

Ben K: Confirmed silence applied. Next step: rebind inference-prod to platform-oncall-policy and remove the contractor alias from the schedule. Will run the small script to patch service binding.

Carla G: FYI that alias removal needs approval from Identity — I'll file the request but we can also add an explicit escalation override on the PD service to the platform policy which should be quicker. Suggest both.

Alice M: I'm going to change the escalation policy now (one-line change) — flip to platform-oncall-policy, then we'll test with a synthetic alert. If that works we'll un-silence and observe.

Ben K: patch applied: `pd service update inference-prod --escalation-policy platform-oncall-policy` — API returned 200.

IncidentBot: synthetic test alert for inference-prod triggered (test-only).

Carla G: received on platform-oncall. Nice. Looks clean now. Removing contractor alias from schedule request submitted (#IAM-4521).

SRE OnCall: un-silencing service and closing duplicate noise lines. Thanks all — I handed the incident to Platform team for mitigation and rollback options.

Alice M: short remediation notes for postmortem: root cause = schedule override + shared email alias leading PD resolution to wrong escalation path. Contributing factor = no explicit service-level escalation override. Customer impact = ~8 minutes of elevated 5xx spikes for a subset of requests (affects customers in eu-west region). Mitigation = emergency silence, rebind to correct policy, remove alias, create test harness for routing.

Ben K: I'll open an incident issue in #postmortems and assign owners (Alice/Carla). Also adding action item to console: add explicit service->policy binding and a runbook snippet for this case.

Carla G: I'll follow up with Identity to deconflict aliases and add a policy to reject schedule entries that reference external/contractor aliases for production schedules.

SRE OnCall: final: no further pages. handing off to Platform-OnCall for follow-up and customer comms. :white_check_mark:

Alice M: assigning incident INC12345 -> PLT-789 (postmortem). Will draft customer impact statement after metric verification. Thanks everyone. :pray:
